text: When the soul is sound and strong, the style too is vigorous, energetic, manly; but if the soul lose its balance, down comes all the rest in ruins.
plain: Everything you do and say rests on how steady your mind is. Lose that and the rest falls apart.

text: The soul is our king. If it be safe, the other functions remain on duty and serve with obedience; but the slightest lack of equilibrium in the soul causes them to waver along with it.
plain: Your mind runs the whole operation. When it wobbles, your habits and your work wobble with it.

text: Now is it not madness, Lucilius, for none of us to reflect that he is mortal? Or frail? Or again that he is but one individual?
plain: You will die, you are fragile, and you are only one person. Act like you know it.

text: Show me any man, however famous; I can tell you what it was that his age forgave in him, and what it was that his age purposely overlooked.
plain: Every famous person has flaws the crowd chose to ignore. Nobody you admire is clean.

text: You should seek what to write, rather than how to write it—and even that not for the purpose of writing but of feeling it, that you may thus make what you have felt more your own and, as it were, set a seal on it.
plain: Care about what you actually feel and think, not how polished it sounds. Make it yours first.

text: The really great man speaks informally and easily; whatever he says, he speaks with assurance rather than with pains.
plain: Real confidence sounds relaxed. Straining to impress is a sign you are not sure.

text: Style is the garb of thought: if it be trimmed, or dyed, or treated, it shows that there are defects and a certain amount of flaws in the mind.
plain: Over-polish is a cover for weakness underneath.

text: We cheat our own eyesight, and when we have overlaid our ceilings with gold, what else is it but a lie in which we take such delight?
plain: We love the gilding on things we know are cheap wood underneath. Wealth is often a nice-looking lie.

text: What tears and toil does money wring from us! Greed is wretched in that which it craves and wretched in that which it wins!
plain: Chasing money hurts, and having more of it does not stop the hurt.

text: The possession of riches means even greater agony of spirit than the acquisition of riches.
plain: Getting rich is stressful. Keeping it is worse.

text: Men complain about their plans and the outcome of their plans; they always prefer what they have failed to win.
plain: People are never happy with what they have. What they missed always looks better.

text: There is no vice which lacks some plea; there is no vice that at the start is not modest and easily entreated; but afterwards the trouble spreads more widely.
plain: Every bad habit starts small and reasonable. It always grows.

text: Every emotion at the start is weak. Afterwards, it rouses itself and gains strength by progress; it is more easy to forestall it than to forgo it.
plain: Stop it at the first spark. Quitting it later is much harder than never letting it start.

text: In so far as we are able, let us step back from slippery places; even on dry ground it is hard enough to take a sturdy stand.
plain: Stay away from situations that tempt you. Standing firm is hard enough without them.

text: And do you know why we have not the power to attain this Stoic ideal? It is because we refuse to believe in our power.
plain: You are not weak. You just do not believe you can do it.

text: We mortals have been endowed with sufficient strength by nature, if only we use this strength, if only we concentrate our powers and rouse them all to help us or at least not to hinder us. The reason is unwillingness, the excuse, inability.
plain: You have enough strength. When you say you cannot, you mean you will not.

text: I think nothing is baser than to pray for death.
plain: Wishing you were dead is the lowest move there is. Stay and fight it out.

text: How foolish it is to practise strokes after you have heard the signal for the fight! Away with all these dummy-weapons; you need armour for a fight to the finish.
plain: Stop rehearsing. The fight has started, so go do the real thing.

text: Nature has not given us such a generous and free-handed space of time that we can have the leisure to waste any of it.
plain: There is not enough time to waste any of it.

text: Out of this time, so short and swift, that carries us away in its flight, of what avail is it to spend the greater part on useless things?
plain: Life is short and fast. Why give most of it to things that do not matter?

text: Make me braver, make me calmer, make me the equal of Fortune, make me her superior.
plain: Wisdom is only worth it if it makes you braver and calmer than whatever life throws at you.

text: Happiness is not, as men think, a greedy thing; it is a lowly thing; for that reason it never gluts a man’s desire.
plain: Happiness is simple and small. That is why more stuff never satisfies the hunger for it.

text: You deem lofty the objects you seek, because you are on a low level and hence far away from them; but they are mean in the sight of him who has reached them.
plain: Goals look huge from far away. Once someone has them, they look small.

text: Most men admire that which deceives them at a distance, and by the crowd good things are supposed to be big things.
plain: The crowd mistakes big for good. Do not trust what only looks great from far away.

text: Enough is never too little, and not-enough is never too much.
plain: If you decide what is enough, you are rich. If you do not, nothing is ever enough.

text: Would you rather have much, or enough? He who has much desires more—a proof that he has not yet acquired enough; but he who has enough has attained that which never fell to the rich man’s lot—a stopping-point.
plain: The man with a lot always wants more. The man with enough is the only one who gets to stop.

text: Money never made a man rich; on the contrary, it always smites men with a greater craving for itself.
plain: Money does not cure wanting money. It feeds it.

text: Hunger is not ambitious; it is quite satisfied to come to an end; nor does it care very much what food brings it to an end.
plain: Your real needs are cheap and easy. It is the extras that cost you.

text: A starving man despises nothing.
plain: Real need makes everything taste good. Comfort is what makes you picky.

text: Carelessness looks like ease, and rashness like bravery.
plain: Some vices dress up as virtues. Look closely before you admire them.

text: The greatest proof of an evil mind is unsteadiness, and continued wavering between pretence of virtue and love of vice.
plain: Flip-flopping between who you claim to be and who you act like is the clearest sign something is off.

text: Believe me, it is a great rôle—to play the rôle of one man. But nobody can be one person except the wise man; the rest of us often shift our masks.
plain: Being the same person every day is rare and hard. Most people swap masks to suit the moment.

text: You should therefore force yourself to maintain to the very end of life’s drama the character which you assumed at the beginning.
plain: Pick who you are and stay him all the way to the end.

text: The failing step does not produce, it merely announces, weariness. The last hour reaches, but every hour approaches, death. Death wears us away, but does not whirl us away.
plain: Death is not one event at the end. It is every hour wearing you down a little.

text: Nothing is enough for us, though we must die some day, or rather, are already dying; for we stand daily nearer the brink, and every hour of time thrusts us on towards the precipice over which we must fall.
plain: We chase more while already dying. Every day brings you closer to the edge.

text: It is indeed consistency that abides; false things do not last.
plain: Only what you do steadily lasts. Fakes fall apart.

text: “Whatever this may be,” he says, “it is my lot; it is rough and it is hard, but I must work diligently at the task.”
plain: Do not curse what you got dealt. It is hard, so do the work anyway.

text: We are more industrious, and we are better men if we anticipate the day and welcome the dawn; but we are base churls if we lie dozing when the sun is high in the heavens, or if we wake up only when noon arrives; and even then to many it seems not yet dawn.
plain: Get up early and meet the day. Sleeping through it makes you smaller.

text: The method of maintaining righteousness is simple; the method of maintaining wickedness is complicated, and has infinite opportunity to swerve.
plain: Doing right is simple. Doing wrong takes endless upkeep.

text: If we follow Nature, all is easy and unobstructed; but if we combat Nature, our life differs not a whit from that of men who row against the current.
plain: Fighting your own nature is rowing upstream. Work with it.

text: To have whatsoever he wishes is in no man’s power; it is in his power not to wish for what he has not, but cheerfully to employ what comes to him.
plain: You cannot get everything you want. You can stop wanting what you lack and use what you have.

text: A great step towards independence is a good-humoured stomach, one that is willing to endure rough treatment.
plain: Getting comfortable with rough conditions makes you free. Do not need it nice.

text: How many things are superfluous we fail to realize until they begin to be wanting; we merely used them not because we needed them but because we had them.
plain: You only find out what you did not need when it is gone. Most of it was habit.

text: Many of our troubles may be explained from the fact that we live according to a pattern, and, instead of arranging our lives according to reason, are led astray by convention.
plain: A lot of your stress comes from copying what everyone else does instead of thinking.

text: There are things which, if done by the few, we should refuse to imitate; yet when the majority have begun to do them, we follow along—just as if anything were more honourable because it is more frequent!
plain: Popular does not mean right. If only a few did it, you would say no.

text: It is not easy to rid the memory of a catching tune; it stays with us, lasts on, and comes back from time to time.
plain: What you hear sticks. Be careful who and what you let into your head.

text: The pleasures take one down hill but one must work upwards toward that which is rough and hard to climb; in the one case let us throw our bodies forward, in the others let us put the check-rein on them.
plain: Pleasure is downhill and easy. Anything worth it is uphill, so lean in.

text: Let us fight in the opposite fashion: let us retreat from the objects that allure, and rouse ourselves to meet the objects that attack.
plain: Back away from temptation and run toward the hard thing.

text: No man is good by chance. Virtue is something which must be learned.
plain: Nobody is good by accident. It is a skill you practice.

text: Poverty is an evil to no man unless he kick against the goads.
plain: Being poor only wrecks you if you fight it with resentment.

text: Death is not an evil; why need you ask? Death alone is the equal privilege of mankind.
plain: Death is not bad, and it is the one thing everybody gets.

text: And what is this Good? I shall tell you: it is a free mind, an upright mind, subjecting other things to itself and itself to nothing.
plain: The best thing is a mind that rules everything else and answers to nothing.

text: Why, pray, do you foster and practise your bodily strength? Nature has granted strength in greater degree to cattle and wild beasts.
plain: Animals beat you at strength and looks. Your edge is your mind, so train that most.

text: You will come to your own when you shall understand that those whom the world calls fortunate are really the most unfortunate of all.
plain: You have arrived when you stop envying the people everyone calls lucky.

text: Be thou sure that God acts in like manner: He does not pet the good man: He tries him, hardens him, and fits him for Himself.
plain: Hard times are not a punishment. They are training for someone worth building.

text: Is there any hard-working man to whom idleness is not a punishment?
plain: If you are built to work, sitting around feels like a sentence.

text: It does not matter what you bear, but how you bear it.
plain: The hardship is not the test. How you carry it is.

text: Those who are surfeited with ease break down not only with labour, but with mere motion and by their own weight.
plain: A soft life makes you collapse at the smallest effort.

text: Unbroken prosperity cannot bear a single blow; but he who has waged an unceasing strife with his misfortunes has gained a thicker skin by his sufferings, yields to no disaster, and even though he fall yet fights on his knee.
plain: Easy wins make you fragile. Struggle makes you tough enough to fight from your knees.

text: Behold a sight worthy to be viewed by a god interested in his own work, behold a pair worthy of a god, a brave man matched with evil fortune, especially if he himself has given the challenge.
plain: A brave person fighting bad luck, especially one they picked, is the best thing there is to watch.

text: A gladiator deems it a disgrace to be matched with an inferior, and knows that to win without danger is to win without glory.
plain: An easy win means nothing. Respect comes from beating something tough.

text: I think you unhappy because you never have been unhappy: you have passed through your life without meeting an antagonist: no one will know your powers, not even you yourself.
plain: Without resistance you never learn what you can do, and neither does anyone else.

text: Valour is greedy of danger, and thinks only of whither it strives to go, not of what it will suffer, since even what it will suffer is part of its glory.
plain: The brave look at where they are going, not at what it will cost. The cost is part of the story.

text: Do not, I beg you, dread those things which the immortal gods apply to our minds like spurs: misfortune is virtue’s opportunity.
plain: Bad luck pushes you forward. It is your chance to prove who you are.

text: Misfortunes press hardest on those who are unacquainted with them: the yoke feels heavy to the tender neck.
plain: Hardship crushes the ones who never practiced it.

text: The recruit turns pale at the thought of a wound: the veteran, who knows that he has often won the victory after losing blood, looks boldly at his own flowing gore.
plain: Rookies panic at pain. Veterans have bled before and won anyway.

text: While all excesses are hurtful, excess of comfort is the most hurtful of all; it affects the brain; it leads men’s minds into vain imaginings; it spreads a thick cloud over the boundaries of truth and falsehood.
plain: Too much comfort rots your thinking more than any other excess.

text: Fortune lashes and mangles us: well, let us endure it: it is not cruelty, it is a struggle, in which the oftener we engage the braver we shall become.
plain: Life beating you up is not cruelty, it is a fight. Each round makes you braver.

text: The strongest part of the body is that which is exercised by the most frequent use: we must entrust ourselves to fortune to be hardened by her against herself: by degrees she will make us a match for herself.
plain: What you use most gets strongest. Face fate often and she makes you her equal.

text: Familiarity with danger leads us to despise it.
plain: The more you face what scares you, the less it scares you.

text: There is no unhappiness in what use has made part of one’s nature: by degrees men find pleasure in doing what they were first driven to do by necessity.
plain: What is hard now becomes normal. Keep doing it and you will start to like it.

text: Fire tries gold, misfortune tries brave men.
plain: Fire shows what gold is. Hard times show who is brave.

text: I am constrained to nothing, I suffer nothing against my will, nor am I God’s slave, but his willing follower, and so much the more because I know that everything is ordained and proceeds according to a law that endures for ever.
plain: When you accept what happens as your own choice, nothing can force you.

text: It is the part of grovellers and cowards to follow the safe track; courage loves a lofty path.
plain: Only cowards play it safe. Take the high, hard road.

text: Despise poverty; no man lives as poor as he was born: despise pain; either it will cease or you will cease: despise death; it either ends you or takes you elsewhere: despise fortune; I have given her no weapon that can reach the mind.
plain: Poverty, pain, death and luck cannot touch your mind unless you let them.

text: I have placed every good thing within your own breasts: it is your good fortune not to need any good fortune.
plain: What matters is inside you. You do not need luck to have it.

text: Do you not blush to spend so long a time in dreading what takes so short a time to do?
plain: Dying takes seconds. You waste years afraid of it.

text: What then? Can heights be reached by a level path?
plain: Nothing great is reached on flat ground. The climb is the deal.

text: The wise man is safe, and no injury or insult can touch him.
plain: If you hold your own mind, other people's attacks cannot reach you.
